az_the_railyard.blurb: The Railyard is a small cluster of crack-focused formations in the West Sedona part of town, at roughly 5,000 feet. Nearly all of its 13 climbs are trad, with one aid line, and the grades centre on 5.10 with a few 5.9s, a couple of 5.11s and one 5.7 starter. Expect hand cracks, fists, off-widths and wide chimneys on sandy, sometimes loose stone, with no bolts to speak of. Most walls face south or southwest, which suits winter days, although the shaded chimneys on the longer lines stay cold. Bring wide gear, solid crack technique and patience for the sand; the walk in crosses a loose, bouldery wash.

az_valerie_s_book_area.blurb: Valerie's Book Area is one broad wall in the Promised Land, a canyon cut into the grassy plains north-east of Prescott near Chino Valley. A prominent right-facing corner splits the face and lends the wall its name. The 13 climbs are a mix of trad and sport, and most are moderate: a handful of easier routes from about 5.4 to 5.7, then several at 5.9 and 5.10, with a single 5.11 and one 5.13 at the top end. The wall sits in shade through winter and picks up afternoon sun the rest of the year, and it is the first big wall you meet on the walk down the canyon.

_expect.name: Mojo Wall and Branching Out Crag

az_mojo_wall_and_branching_out_crag.blurb: These two small crags sit on the mid-mountain stretch of Mount Lemmon near Tucson, around 7,500 feet, within a couple of minutes of the San Pedro Vista overlook. The 13 routes mix trad and sport and run steep, with most graded 5.11 and the rest split between 5.10 and 5.12. The rock faces north, south and west, and steeper lines tend to be clean while the gentler north and west sections can be lichen-furred. The rocks jut from a very steep hillside, so moving between faces is awkward and anything dropped can roll a long way. Climbers on the visible lines can be watched from the overlook.

az_heaven_s_gate.blurb: Heaven's Gate is a compact set of buttresses, fins and walls at different heights in Lower Devil's Canyon, part of the Refuge in Queen Creek Canyon near Superior. A narrow corridor between formations gives it the name, and the entrance is hidden enough that a little exploring may be needed. Its 13 routes lean trad, with a few sport lines, and most sit between 5.9 and 5.10 with one 5.7, one 5.8 and a single 5.11. Quality of the stone changes with how much sun a face gets. The walk-in follows the trail toward Easter Island Head and then turns off at a rock formation.

az_punch_and_judy_towers.blurb: Punch and Judy Towers is a south-facing cliff just down the Catalina Highway from the Windy Point overlook on Mount Lemmon, at about 6,000 feet. It holds 13 routes, eight sport and five trad, and they are steep for the mountain: mostly 5.11 and 5.12, with a lone 5.9, two 5.10s and one 5.13. Strong sun makes it a cool-season choice, and it gets uncomfortable on hot summer days. The walk from the roadside parking is only a few hundred feet, but Windy Point is a busy tourist stop, so the area draws plenty of traffic.

az_wall_of_the_flying_scorpions.blurb: A small northwest-facing wall on the Lower Highway of Mount Lemmon, in the Sonoran Desert foothills above Tucson at roughly 4,500 feet. All 13 routes are bolted sport climbs of about 40 to 80 feet, built around edging on banded gneiss, mostly from 5.9 to 5.11 with one 5.8. A leaning pillar at the south end gives the hardest test. The stone feels newer and a bit loose in places, and a helmet is a good idea. The walk follows the ridge down from the parking area and then contours across to the cliff.

az_it_cliff.blurb: It Cliff is a small overhanging outcrop on the Lower Highway of Mount Lemmon, reached from the Molino Basin lot. Of its 13 routes, most are sport with a couple of trad lines, including the well-known crack. Grades cluster around 5.11 and 5.12, with just two 5.9s. The lines mostly face north and north-east, so the cliff stays shaded for much of the day and is pleasant when other lower-mountain walls are hot. The approach follows an established path south, then a faint trail over the wash to the overhung wall.

az_left_hand_wall.blurb: Left Hand Wall is a moderate crag in the Hairpin Turn Area of Mount Lemmon's Lower Highway, near Tucson at about 3,200 feet, which keeps it climbable from late autumn into early spring. The 13 routes split between sport and trad, and many lines need both draws and a rack. Grades are friendly: mostly 5.8, with a few 5.9s and a handful of easier lines. The wall faces east and is sunny until mid-afternoon. The angle is often less than vertical with horizontal banding, but the rock is loose in spots, so belayers should wear helmets. Watch for bees near the base.
